subject: International data guardrails: RFI responses and DPA annex (Helias Medical)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@heliasmed.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliasmed.com
Date: 2028-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: international data transfers & technical controls - Helias questionnaire

Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — attached is Helias's standard international-transfer & security controls questionnaire. We are evaluating vendors for a pilot in Q1; primary concerns are: EU patient PII residency, evidence of technical safeguards (encryption in transit + at rest), and an auditable DPA annex that maps subprocessors.

High-level timing: can you provide a written response to the questionnaire and any supporting evidence by EOD 2028-09-20? If you have a DPA annex template we can review, please include it.

Specific asks in the questionnaire (short):
- Confirmation of processor role and any controller-controller scenarios
- Cross-border mechanisms (SCCs, DPF, adequacy) and fallback routing
- KMS/HSM details and key custody options
- List of subprocessors and subprocessor contract model
- Retention and audit log windows (we require 12 months of immutable audit logs for this pilot)

Attachments: Helias-International-Transfer-RFI-2028.pdf (questionnaire)

Best,
Elena
Head of Procurement
Helias Medical Systems

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international data transfers & technical controls - Helias questionnaire (draft responses)

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Helias's questionnaire (attached). I'm drafting a concise response that covers: DPA annex options, cross-border mechanisms we support, and evidence we can provide (SOC2 excerpts, DPF mapping, subprocessors). Quick notes / asks below so we can finalize by 9/20: 

1) Controller vs Processor: Helias asks us to confirm. For the pilot we act as processor; however, if they enable any pipeline feature that stores customer metadata for model tuning, we need to note the controller-controller nuance and our opt-out. Ben, could you confirm the product features they intend to use in the pilot so we can state this precisely?

2) Cross-border mechanism: We should outline primary approach = EU-hosted tenancy (option A), fallback = SCCs with documented transfer map (option B). Legal: is the DPF acceptance an option we can commit to, or should we avoid promising DPF certification? Marissa, please advise on whether we can state "supports DPF-proofing steps" vs claiming DPF compliance.

3) KMS / key custody: We'll offer customer-managed KMS via Azure/AWS/GCP + HSM option for dedicated/private deployments. Draft language attached (DPA annex section 4.2) — please review.

4) Audit log retention: Helias asks for 12 months immutable logs. Our hosted plan currently keeps 12 months of token-level traces in the Console (configurable). Is the term "immutable" OK if we add a retention SLA and WORM-backed object store for dedicated/private? 

Attachments I'm proposing to send to Helias as part of the response: redwood-dpf-guardrails-summary.pdf (short), draft DPA annex, SOC2 excerpt stub.

If you both approve, I'll send to Elena with the attachments and a DocuSign link for the annex by EOD 9/20.

Thanks —
Soojin
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international data transfers & technical controls - Helias questionnaire (edits)

Thanks Soojin — I reviewed the draft. A few edits / requests before we send externally: 

- DPF language: do not state we are DPF-certified. Instead say: "Redwood is actively aligning with EU transfer frameworks and can provide DPF-aligned documentation upon request; primary enforcement mechanism will be regional hosting and SCCs where applicable."

- SCCs vs adequacy: We can promise SCCs + regional hosting for the pilot. Do not promise adequacy decisions.

- Audit logs: confirm we can offer 12 months of immutable audit logs for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, say "configurable retention; standard retention is 90 days; 12 months available under enterprise contract."

- KMS: add optional Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) phrasing and mention HSM-backed key storage for Private/Dedicated. 

- Subprocessors: include link to live subprocessor list (we keep it updated in the Console) and add an offer to provide a snapshot export for Helias procurement. Procurement typically wants names + locations + datacenter regions.

Ben: any pricing implication for the 12-month log retention or BYOK we should flag to the prospect? If so, add a brief note in the cover email: "additional enterprise services may incur fees."

Once we agree, Soojin send as final. I'll be on standby for negotiations.

—Marissa
Director, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@heliasmed.com>, procurement@heliasmed.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-20T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international data transfers & technical controls - Helias questionnaire (Redwood response)

Elena —

Thanks for the questionnaire and timeline. Please find our consolidated responses below and three short attachments: 1) Redwood international data guardrails (PDF) — a concise mapping to your RFI, 2) Draft DPA annex you can review in DocuSign (Word), 3) SOC2 report excerpt (redacted) as an evidence stub. Attachments referenced at the bottom and a DocuSign link is included for the annex.

Summary (top-line)
- Role: For the pilot, Redwood will act as Processor to Helias. We are prepared to include explicit processor-only language in the DPA annex. If Helias chooses features that require controller-level decisions (e.g., model training with customer data), those will be handled under a mutually agreed addendum.
- Cross-border approach: Primary option = EU-region tenancy for production data (we can pin the pilot to an EU region). Secondary mechanism = SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) with a documented transfer map. We will not represent Redwood as DPF-certified at this time, but we provide DPF-aligned mapping artifacts and can work with you on the proofing steps.
- KMS & key custody: BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and an HSM option available under enterprise terms. Key rotation & separation of duties language included in section 4.2 of the annex.
- Audit logs & retention: Dedicated and Private deployments can support 12 months WORM-style audit retention on request (enterprise feature). Hosted default retention is 90 days; 12 months can be provisioned under an enterprise contract (potential additional fee). Logs include token-level traces and admin actions and are exportable for audit.
- Subprocessors: Live subprocessor list is published in the Console; we will provide a snapshot export that includes names, primary region, and role. We require subprocessors to sign contracts with equivalent data obligations.

Attached evidence & next steps
- Attachments: redwood-dpf-guardrails-summary.pdf (high-level mapping), dpa-annex-helias-draft.docx (word, DocuSign-ready), soc2-report-excerpt-stub.pdf (redacted, control mapping).
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e — this envelope contains the proposed DPA annex. We recommend review by your legal team and, if acceptable, completion to accelerate the pilot kickoff.
- Additional offers: we can provide a dedicated snapshot of audit logs and a subprocessor export for procurement review. If Helias wants a dedicated EU-only tenancy for the pilot (recommended), we can scope cost & timeline in a separate SOW.

Please let me know if you want this as a one-page Q&A mapping to the exact Helias questionnaire fields — happy to populate the provided PDF mapping to their original questions.

Best regards,

Soojin Lee
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
